sentences.text: Tikisuchus possessed a skull that was exceptionally large compared to other rauisuchids, reaching a length of approximately 40% of the presacral vertebral column.
Its jaws held large, recurved, and serrated teeth, while two rows of osteoderms, or bony scutes, ran along its back.
These rectangular osteoderms articulated tightly with adjacent ones in an imbricate pattern.
Tikisuchus was the first rauisuchid fossil discovered in Asia, yet only one specimen, ISI R 305, is known today.
This single find contains the skull and some postcranial bones of a young individual.
The type species Tikisuchus romeri was named to honor the American paleontologist Alfred Romer.
Tikisuchus was a large terrestrial predator that likely shared its habitat with theropod dinosaurs.
Potential prey for Tikisuchus included rhynchosaurs, trilophosaurs, dicynodonts, and aetosaurs.
Tikisuchus is classified as an extinct genus of rauisuchid archosauromorph belonging to the family Rauisuchidae.
Tikisuchus lived during the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic, between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
Recent studies debate the cause of rauisuchid decline, suggesting dinosaurs only became dominant after the Triassic-Jurassic extinction removed competing large archosaurs.
